- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.3) and forecast is significantly below true outcome, adjust upward by 1–2% of the forecasted range to capture bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.1) and forecast is overestimated, reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overreaction to bearish signals.  
- If forecast shows a sharp spike followed by a steep drop, reduce the immediate post-spike values by 5–10% to account for overcorrection or lag.  
- For 30-day horizons, if true outcome is consistently higher than forecast in the first 5–7 days, apply a “mean reversion” bias: add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for days 8–15 to align with recent upward trend.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (≤ 0.1) and forecast is consistently high, apply a “lag correction”: subtract 1–2% from forecast for days 10–20 to reflect delayed market reaction.  
- When sentiment is volatile (fluctuating between 0.1–0.4) and forecast is erratic, use a smoothing filter: average the last 3–5 forecast values before applying the next prediction.
